# When Does Personality Composition Matter for Multi-Agent LLM Teams?

> A COLM 2026 paper testing whether personality prompts that measurably shift LLM agent communication actually change objective task outcomes. They shift communication everywhere (Cohen's d from −1.17 to −12.39), but outcomes only degrade when the task is unstructured: structured code artifacts buffer the effect ("artifact-mediated buffering"), while open-ended research and competitive bargaining suffer. Low agreeableness collapses bargaining agreement from ~40% to ≤1%.

Paper: "When Does Personality Composition Matter for Multi-Agent LLM Teams?" by Aryan Keluskar, Amrita Bhattacharjee, and Huan Liu (School of Computing & AI, Arizona State University). Published at the Conference on Language Modeling (COLM 2026), San Francisco, October 6–9, 2026.

## Key facts

- Four frontier models evaluated: Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-4o, Grok-3, DeepSeek V3.1, on coding (3 agents), research (5 agents), and buyer–seller bargaining (2 agents) from MultiAgentBench.
- Personality shaped with Goldberg's bipolar adjective markers for the Big Five (Serapio-García et al. 2025 protocol); primary conditions low-agreeableness (level 2) and high-agreeableness (level 8).
- Low-A drives every model to a disagreement-dominated communication profile (exploration fraction φ ≈ 0.93) — but in coding, milestone completion is essentially unchanged for 3 of 4 models (Claude 12.1→12.4, d=0.06).
- Unstructured tasks are exposed: research milestones drop up to 66%; bargaining agreement collapses from ~40% baseline to ≤1% under low-A across all three tested models. High-A roughly doubles agreement.
- Low-A agents still negotiate (GPT-4o revises offers in 90% of runs vs. 95% at baseline) but call accept_offer in only 1% of runs: agreeableness acts on the final accept decision.
- Only agreeableness matters: conscientiousness and openness ablations leave communication near baseline; high-A is null because RLHF-trained models are already cooperative.
- A neutral paraphrase of the low-A prompt ("direct, candid, skeptical of consensus...") attenuates the shift and removes cross-model convergence, but a model-specific residual persists: loaded Goldberg adjectives partly measure prompt-toxicity sensitivity.
- Design recommendation: deploy low agreeableness as a bounded, lead-position critic, not a team-wide trait.
